2. Heard learned counsel for the Appellant who has been engaged this case with the help of Orissa High Court Legal Aid Service Committee.

sentences.text: The Present appeal has been filed on the basis of a prisoner's petition on 26.10.2024 with a delay of 255 days.

3. On perusal of the case record, it appears that the Appellant who is in jail custody seeks to challenge the judgment dated 07.11.2023 passed in Special Case No.60 of 2017 which corresponds to T.C. No.86 of 2021 arising out of Nayakote P.S. Case No.27 dated 28.06.2017 by the Adhoc Addl.
District & Sessions Judge (FTSC),Keonjhar thereby convicting the Petitioner for commission of an offence punishable under Section 366/ 376(2)(n) of the I.P.C. read with Section 6 of the POCSO Act and he has been sentenced to undergo RI for a period of ten years and to pay a fine of Rs.20,000/-.
Initially the Petitioner was arrested on 28.07.2017, thereafter he was released on bail on 27.01.2018.
Thereafter, the petitioner has again been taken back to the custody from the date of judgment,
07.11.2023, and he is languishing in custody since that date.
4.

Taking into consideration the fact that the Appellant is in custody and this appeal has been preferred with the help of the Legal Aid, this Court is inclined to condone the delay of 255 days in presenting this appeal before this Court.

10. Extra copy of the appeal memo be served on learned counsel for the State-Respondent, who shall make any endeavour to serve appeal memo on the informant/victim and obtain a confirmation of such service of appeal memo by the next date.

11. List this matter in the week commencing 2nd February, 2026.
12.

13. As an interim measure the realization of fine amount awarded by the Court below shall remain stayed till the next date.

14. Heard.
